chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Sahl ibn Zyad al-Adamy, from Muhammad ibn Sin'an, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, from Yunus ibn Abi Zibyan, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me:

O Yunus! Fear God and believe in His Messenger.' I said, 'I believe in God and His Messenger.' Then he said: 'The easy religion of Muhammad consists of: establishing prayer, paying alms-tax, fasting the month of Ramadan, performing Hajj to the Sacred House, obedience to the Imam, and fulfilling the rights of the believers. Indeed, whoever withholds the right of a believer, God will make him stand on his feet for five hundred years on the Day of Resurrection until rivers flow from his sweat. Then a caller from near God, Exalted is His Glory, will announce: 'This is the oppressor who withheld God's right.' He will be rebuked for forty years, then he will be ordered into the Fire of Hell.'
ai.seo_question: What are the six characteristics of the easy religion of Muhammad according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expands the traditional five pillars by integrating obedience to the Imam and fulfilling the rights of believers (*huquq al-nas*) as essential components of the 'easy religion' (*al-mahmudiyya al-samha*). The narration highlights the severe eschatological consequence of withholding a believer's due right, describing a unique punishment of standing for five hundred years in sweat before being rebuked and cast into Hell, underscoring the Shia emphasis on social justice and the spiritual weight of interpersonal obligations.
